Blessing of the Spirits.description: Beginning at 4th level, the spirit shaman can conduct a ritual that bestows a protective ward upon herself. She enters a meditative trance, journeying spiritually for 10 minutes. This ward applies only to the spirit shaman personally and cannot be performed on behalf of others. The resulting protection operates identically to protection from evil, but shields against spirits rather than evil creatures, and persists until dismissed or dispelled. If the effect is dispelled, the spirit shaman may simply repeat the 10-minute ritual to restore it.

Chastise Spirits.description: From 2nd level onward, the spirit shaman can channel divine power from her spirit patrons to harm hostile spirits. As a standard action, she inflicts 1d6 damage per shaman level on every spirit within a 30-foot radius. Each affected spirit may attempt a Will save (DC 10 + shaman level + Charisma modifier) to reduce the damage by half. Against incorporeal creatures, the spirit shaman bypasses the usual 50% miss chance entirely -- the energy strikes automatically. This ability can be used a number of times per day equal to 3 + the spirit shaman's Charisma modifier.

Detect Spirits.description: Through her spirit guide's heightened perception, the spirit shaman can sense spirits in her vicinity. She may use this as a spell-like ability at will. It operates identically to detect undead, except that it reveals creatures classified as spirits instead.

Exorcism.description: From 13th level, as a full-round action, the spirit shaman can drive a possessing entity out of the body it occupies (such as a ghost using malevolence). She rolls a class level check, adding her Charisma modifier if applicable, against a DC equal to 10 + the possessor's Hit Dice + its Charisma modifier (if any). If the check meets or exceeds the DC, the possessing creature is expelled, with outcomes determined by its particular method of possession. A spirit expelled this way is barred from possessing that same individual for 24 hours.

Favored of the Spirits.description: At 19th level, the spirit shaman can perform a protective rite that shields her from death. The rite takes 8 hours to complete, and the spirit shaman must sacrifice a portion of her life energy, expending 1,000 experience points. The protection remains active until dismissed or discharged. While this rite is in effect, if the spirit shaman drops to 0 or fewer hit points, or if any of her ability scores is reduced to 0, she instantly gains the benefit of a heal spell (with a caster level equal to her spirit shaman level). This healing takes effect immediately, even if the triggering blow would have reduced her below -10 hit points, potentially saving her from outright death. Once triggered, the protection ends, and the spirit shaman must perform the rite again to regain this benefit.

Follow the Guide.description: At 5th level, the spirit shaman's spirit guide assists her in resisting mental influence. Whenever she fails a saving throw against an enchantment spell or effect, she may retry the save once, 1 round later, at the same DC. Only one additional attempt is granted per failed save.

Ghost Warrior.description: Starting at 6th level, any weapon the spirit shaman wields gains the ghost touch property for as long as she holds it. In addition, she becomes more resilient against the touch attacks of incorporeal beings, applying her full Armor Class rather than just her touch AC when defending against an incorporeal creature's touch attack.

Guide Magic.description: From 10th level, as a free action, the spirit shaman can delegate concentration on a spell or spell-like ability to her spirit guide. While the guide maintains the spell, the spirit shaman is free to act normally. The guide can sustain concentration on only one spell at a time. When Concentration checks are required to maintain the spell, the guide uses the spirit shaman's normal Concentration modifier. However, the guide does not need to make Concentration checks due to external disruptions such as the spirit shaman taking damage. Because the spirit guide has no physical presence, it cannot be targeted or interrupted by other creatures.

Recall Spirit.description: At 11th level, the spirit shaman gains the power to summon back the departing spirit of a creature that has just died, reconnecting it to its body. She can use this ability once per week, and it must be employed within 1 round of the creature's death. This works like raise dead, except the restored creature suffers no level loss, no Constitution loss, and no loss of prepared spells.

Spells.description: The spirit shaman casts divine spells drawn from the druid spell list. She can cast any spell she has retrieved for the day without needing to prepare it in advance, similar to how a bard or sorcerer casts known spells spontaneously. Retrieving or casting a spell requires a minimum Wisdom score of 10 + the spell's level. The saving throw DC for her spells equals 10 + spell level + her Charisma modifier. Like other casters, she is limited to a certain number of spells per day at each level, as shown in the class table, and gains bonus spells per day from a high Wisdom score. Although the spirit shaman knows only a limited number of spells at a time (like a sorcerer), she can change which spells she knows each day. During her daily meditation to recover spell slots, her spirit guide ventures into the spirit world and returns with knowledge of specific druid spells she can use that day. She may then cast any retrieved spell freely, as long as she has unused spell slots of the appropriate level. For instance, a 3rd-level spirit shaman retrieves three 0-level, two 1st-level, and one 2nd-level spell. She can cast 0-level spells five times, 1st-level spells four times, and her 2nd-level spell twice throughout the day, mixing and matching her retrieved spells in any combination that does not exceed her daily allotment for each level. Metamagic feats must be applied at the time of retrieval, not at the time of casting. For example, she could retrieve an empowered flame strike in a 6th-level slot; every time she casts flame strike that day, it uses a 6th-level slot and is always empowered. She could also retrieve both a normal flame strike in a 4th-level slot and an empowered version in a 6th-level slot to have both options available. Unlike other spontaneous casters, spirit shamans do not suffer increased casting times when applying metamagic. The spirit shaman must designate a specific time each day when she spends 1 hour in quiet meditation to regain her spells and negotiate with the spirits for the particular spells she will know that day.

Spirit Form.description: At 9th level, the spirit shaman learns to temporarily transform into a spirit. Once per day, as a standard action, she can become incorporeal for up to 1 minute. In this state, she gains all benefits of the incorporeal subtype: immunity to nonmagical attacks, a 50% chance to avoid damage from corporeal sources, and the ability to pass through solid objects. She loses any armor or natural armor bonus to AC but gains a deflection bonus equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum +1). She has no effective Strength score against corporeal creatures or objects and cannot physically attack them, but she can deliver a melee touch attack (using her Dexterity modifier on the attack roll) that deals 1d6 damage to corporeal targets. This attack counts as a magic weapon for purposes of bypassing damage reduction. At 15th level, she can use spirit form twice per day. At 20th level, the daily uses increase to three.

Spirit Guide.description: Every spirit shaman possesses a spirit guide -- a manifestation of the spirit world that exists entirely within her mind and soul. The shaman and her guide share all perceptions and experiences as though they were a single being. Unlike a familiar, the spirit guide is not a separate creature; only the spirit shaman can perceive or interact with it. The spirit guide grants the spirit shaman heightened awareness, providing the Alertness feat. It also unlocks further abilities at 5th level (Follow the Guide) and 10th level (Guide Magic). The spirit shaman selects the guide's form at 1st level, typically based on the qualities it symbolizes. The specific appearance of the guide is a matter of personal choice and provides no mechanical advantages or drawbacks.

Spirit Journey.description: From 17th level, the spirit shaman can physically transport herself into the spirit realm. This works like shadow walk, but she can only bring herself. She does not need to be in a shadowy area to activate it, and she travels through the Plane of Spirits rather than the Plane of Shadow. This ability can be used once per day.

Spirit Who Walks.description: Upon reaching 20th level, the spirit shaman merges permanently with the spirit world. She is henceforth considered a fey rather than a humanoid for all purposes involving spells and magical effects. She also gains damage reduction 5/cold iron.

Warding of the Spirits.description: From 7th level, the spirit shaman can perform a daily protective rite that shields herself and her allies from hostile spirits. The ritual takes 1 minute to complete. The resulting ward persists for 10 minutes per level and functions identically to magic circle against evil, except that it offers protection against spirits.

Weaken Spirits.description: At 16th level, the spirit shaman gains the option to use her chastise spirits ability to strip away spirits' defenses rather than simply dealing damage. A weakened spirit loses its spell resistance and any damage reduction that can be overcome by magic, silver, cold iron, or aligned weapons (though DR overcome only by adamantine or DR with no bypass remains unaffected). A weakened incorporeal spirit also loses its immunity to nonmagical attacks, its 50% chance to ignore corporeal damage, and its ability to pass through solid objects. To use this option, the spirit shaman sacrifices a portion of the chastise spirits damage: for every 3d6 of damage she forgoes, affected spirits are weakened for 1 round. For example, a 16th-level spirit shaman normally deals 16d6 damage, but could reduce the damage to 7d6 in order to weaken the targets for 3 rounds instead. Spirits that succeed on their Will save against the chastise spirits damage avoid the weakening effect entirely, though they still take half damage.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: The spirit shaman is proficient with clubs, daggers, darts, hand axes, javelins, longspears, quarterstaves, shortspears, spears, slings, shortbows, throwing axes, as well as light armor and shields. These represent the typical armaments of the tribal cultures from which spirit shamans originate.

Wild Empathy.description: Drawing on her connection to animal spirits, the spirit shaman can use body language, vocalizations, and demeanor to shift the disposition of an animal (any creature of the animal type). This works like a Diplomacy check to improve a person's attitude. She rolls 1d20 and adds her spirit shaman level plus her Charisma modifier to determine the result. Domesticated animals typically start as indifferent, while wild animals are generally unfriendly. Both the spirit shaman and the animal must be able to observe one another, requiring them to be within 30 feet under normal circumstances. Influencing an animal in this manner generally takes about 1 minute, though it can take more or less time depending on circumstances. This ability does not work on magical beasts.

classFeatures.description: A spirit shaman knows how to vanish bodily into the spirit world beginning at 17th level. This ability functions like the spell shadow walk, except that a spirit shaman can only transport herself. She need not use the ability in a shadowy area, and she travels through the Plane of Spirits, not the Plane of Shadows. A spirit shaman can use this ability once per day.
classFeatures.name: Spirit Journey

classFeatures.description: At 19th level, a spirit shaman learns how to perform a special rite that guards her from death. Performing the rite requires 8 hours, and the spirit shaman must bargain away part of her life force, expending 1,000 experience points. The rite's effect lasts until it is dismissed or discharged. While under the protection of this rite, a spirit shaman instantly receives the benefit of a heal spell (caster level equal to her spirit shaman level) if she is reduced to 0 hit points or lower or has any ability score reduced to 0. The spirit shaman receives the spell's effect immediately, even if reduced to -10 hit points or lower by an enemy attack, and thus may survive a blow that otherwise would have killed her. The rite's protection is discharged once it is triggered, and the spirit shaman must perform a new rite to use this ability again.
classFeatures.name: Favored of the Spirits

classFeatures.description: At 20th level, a spirit shaman becomes one with the spirit world. She is forevermore treated as a fey instead of a humanoid for purposes of spells and magical effects. Additionally, she gains damage reduction 5/cold iron.
classFeatures.name: Spirit Who Walks

raw.description: By bargaining with living spirits, the spirit shaman gains power over the natural world and mighty divine magic.
raw.name: Spirit Shaman
